reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n with n > 0, let O(n) be the full group of real n by n orthogonal matrices, equipped with its inherited matrix Borel structure, and let mu be its canonical Haar probability measure, obtained by the Haar construction normalized on the whole group. Define C_plus = {O in O(n) : det(O) = 1} and C_minus = {O in O(n) : det(O) = -1}. Then mu(C_plus) = 1/2 and mu(C_minus) = 1/2, with these values interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals. Furthermore, each of the actual measures nu_plus = 2 times (mu restricted to C_plus) and nu_minus = 2 times (mu restricted to C_minus), on the original carrier O(n), is a probability measure. Explicitly, for every Borel set A in O(n), nu_plus(A) = 2 mu(A intersect C_plus) and nu_minus(A) = 2 mu(A intersect C_minus), and nu_plus(O(n)) = nu_minus(O(n)) = 1. All four assertions are conclusions under the sole non-typing hypothesis n > 0. In particular, the result includes n = 1 and makes no assertion for n = 0.
objects: The full real orthogonal matrix group O(n); its actual canonical whole-group-normalized Haar probability mu; determinant level sets C_plus and C_minus at 1 and -1; the actual restricted and scaled measures nu_plus = 2 times mu.restrict(C_plus) and nu_minus = 2 times mu.restrict(C_minus). These restricted measures are genuine measures, not freely assigned symbols or caller-supplied measure families.
domains: n ranges over natural numbers, with n > 0. Matrix row and column indices are Fin n and matrix entries lie in the real numbers. O ranges over the full real orthogonal group, equipped with the inherited matrix Borel structure. C_plus and C_minus are subsets of this group. mu, nu_plus, and nu_minus are measures on this same full carrier with values in the extended nonnegative reals. Determinants are real; the mass 1/2 and scaling factor 2 are extended nonnegative real constants.
quantifiers: Universally quantify over each natural number n and each proof hn of 0 < n. mu, C_plus, and C_minus are locally defined from n, not additional universally quantified or existentially chosen data. The four conclusions are simultaneous. The Borel test set A used in the explicit restriction formula is arbitrary and only explicates the actual restricted measures.
assumptions: The only non-typing hypothesis is 0 < n. The canonical Haar probability and standard determinant interpretation are supplied by the approved definitions. No half-mass identity, probability property of a scaled restriction, determinant witness, partition, invariance, integrability, or Gaussian-family property is assumed of the caller.
conclusion: mu(C_plus) = (2 in the extended nonnegative reals) inverse and mu(C_minus) = (2 in the extended nonnegative reals) inverse, and both 2 times mu.restrict(C_plus) and 2 times mu.restrict(C_minus) have total mass 1 and hence are probability measures on O(n). These are four conjunctive conclusions. For Borel A the scaled restrictions have values 2 mu(A intersect C_plus) and 2 mu(A intersect C_minus), respectively.
scopes: All local definitions and all four conclusions lie inside the universal quantification over positive natural dimension n. Both restricted measures retain the full orthogonal group as their carrier; restricting a measure does not change the domain to a subtype. Positivity includes the endpoint n = 1, where O(1) consists of the matrices [1] and [-1], so each has mu-mass 1/2 and each scaled restriction has mass 1 at its respective matrix. Dimension n = 0 is outside the statement. There is no claim about Gaussian objects or an additional dimension parameter.
constant_dependencies: The finite constants 2, its inverse 1/2, determinant levels 1 and -1, and probability total mass 1 are fixed universally, independent of n and hn. mu and the determinant level sets depend on n through O(n); nu_plus and nu_minus are determined by mu and the corresponding sets. No unspecified constants, choices of a Haar normalization, free scalar, determinant witness, or external parameters occur.
